title: The sensitivity theorem
statement:
The sensitivity theorem says that for all $n\ge 1$ and all Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to \{-1,1\}$, we have
	

$$
s(f)\ge \sqrt{\deg (f)}.
$$

technical_disposition: The displayed inequality is explicitly a theorem. Producing another proof is not discovery credit; real-valued sensitivity and what qualifies as reasonable have no specified target. Scaling alone defeats naive numerical sensitivity extensions.

title: A stronger BSG theorem
statement:
Let $A\subset G$, and suppose $E(A)\geq \frac{|A|^3}{K}$. Then there is a set $A'\subset A$ so that 
$$
|A'|\geq \frac{|A|}{K^{100}},
$$

$$
|A'+A'|\leq K^{100}|A'|,
$$

$$
\frac{E(A')}{|A'|^3}\geq \frac{E(A)}{|A|^3}
$$

Can we moreover obtain the following?

$$
\frac{E(A')}{|A'|^3}\geq \frac{E(A)}{|A|^3} \left(\frac{|A|}{|A'|}\right)^{\frac{1}{100}}
$$
quantifiers_and_scope: Every finite A in source ambient G with energy >=|A|^3/K has a polynomial-size, polynomial-doubling subset with normalized energy gain (|A|/|A'|)^(1/100).
technical_disposition: Ordinary BSG does not automatically enforce monotone normalized energy with the stronger gain. A subgroup has no obstruction since A'=A works; a generic energy-increment sketch still needs loss accounting at every step. No full-scope argument established.
